title: INSTANT: Compressing Gradients and Activations for Resource-Efficient Training
claim: Training can save memory and compute by storing compressed activations in the forward pass and running low-rank backward computation.
layout: Left legend box, two horizontal lanes (forward top, backward bottom) linked by a central memory bar
description: A wide, flat diagram with a rounded legend box on the left. The legend explains the arrows: a green arrow for Forward, a red arrow pointing left for Backward, and a black arrow for INSTANT Compression. The top lane is green. It shows activations A_i, A_{i+1} and A_{i+2} flowing rightward through light-green 'Full-rank Forward' boxes. At each stage a small black compression bar produces a compact version Â_i or Â_{i+1}, which drops down by arrow into a wide blue 'Memory' bar in the center. The bottom lane is red. Gradients ∂L/∂A_{i+2}, ∂L/∂A_{i+1} and ∂L/∂A_i flow leftward through red 'Low-rank Backward' boxes. Each gradient passes through a black compression bar. Dashed arrows carry the stored Â from Memory into the backward boxes. The eye goes first to the large central Memory bar, then to the green and red lanes.
caption: INSTANT performs compression on activations and gradients: In the forward pass (Green), activation Ai normally propagates in full-rank space while its compact version ˆAi is saved for the backpropagation to reduce memory consumption. In the backward pass (Red), the gradient for the output ∂L ∂Ai+1 is compressed to a low-rank version
abstract: Deep learning has advanced at an unprecedented pace. This progress has led to a significant increase in its complexity. However, despite extensive research on accelerating inference, training deep models directly within a resource-constrained budget remains a considerable challenge due to its high computational and memory requirements. In this paper, we introduce INSTANT (compressIng gradieNtS and acTivAtions for resource-efficieNt Training), a method designed to address both the computational and the memory bottlenecks when training. INSTANT reduces resource demands during backpropagation by projecting gradients and activations into a low-rank subspace and performing computation within that compressed representation. Experimental results demonstrate that INSTANT achieves a $15\times$ reduction in computational cost and $32\times$ reduction in activation memory with negligible impact on model performance. The code will be made publicly available upon the paper's acceptance.
